cases.description: You are a 35-year-old man with iron deficiency anemia and ankylosing spondylitis, currently taking ferrous sulfate, artificial tear drops, and indomethacin. You presented with itchy, watery eyes and frequent sneezing over the past week, which is similar to an episode you experienced last spring. Your physical examination shows redness in both of your eyes along with watery discharge, though your vision remains normal and your pupils are equal and reactive. Based on these findings, you are experiencing allergic conjunctivitis.

cases.description:
You are a 39-year-old man with a five-year history of unmanaged high blood pressure, a five-year habit of smoking one pack of cigarettes daily, and recent cocaine use starting two weeks ago.

You came to the emergency department due to increasingly severe chest discomfort and nausea that began thirty minutes ago at a bar, with the pain spreading to your upper abdomen. Upon evaluation, you were sweating profusely and showing signs of significant distress. Based on your history and symptoms, your diagnosis is cocaine-associated chest pain.

answers.text:
Amlodipine 5mg daily (full dose)
Reason: Prevents hypertensive crisis and cardiac strain during heavy labor despite financial barriers.

TRIAGE_LEVEL: Urgent

CARE_SETTING: Outpatient

CT Angiography (CTA) of Chest and Abdomen
Reason: This is the definitive procedure to immediately rule out life-threatening aortic dissection given the patient's belly pain and hypertension.

TRIAGE_LEVEL: Emergent

CARE_SETTING: Inpatient

Intravenous antihypertensive therapy (e.g., Esmolol, Labetalol, Nitroprusside)
Reason: Immediate reduction of heart rate and blood pressure is critical to prevent further aortic tearing or rupture.

TRIAGE_LEVEL: RESUSCITATION

CARE_SETTING: INPATIENT

Benzodiazepines and Vasodilators
Reason: To reduce sympathomimetic-induced hypertension, tachycardia, and coronary vasospasm while avoiding beta-blockers.

TRIAGE_LEVEL: EMERGENT

CARE_SETTING: INPATIENT

Continuous cardiac and neurological monitoring
Reason: The patient lives alone and reports cognitive impairment, increasing the risk of missing life-threatening "red flag" symptoms during the cocaine washout period.

TRIAGE_LEVEL: EMERGENT

CARE_SETTING: INPATIENT

Continued Amlodipine therapy
Reason: Essential for lowering systemic vascular resistance and preventing further hypertensive heart strain.

TRIAGE_LEVEL: URGENT

CARE_SETTING: OUTPATIENT

Blood pressure medication (beta-blocker) + aspirin
Reason: Essential post-cocaine chest pain care; prevents recurrent cardiac events and is low-cost generic.

TRIAGE_LEVEL: URGENT

CARE_SETTING: OUTPATIENT

Cardiology evaluation with coronary imaging (CTA or stress testing)
Reason: Cocaine-induced vasospasm and coronary artery disease require specialist assessment and imaging to rule out structural damage.

TRIAGE_LEVEL: URGENT

CARE_SETTING: OUTPATIENT

Cardiac monitoring with serial troponin and EKG
Reason: Cocaine-induced acute coronary syndrome suspected; continuous assessment needed to rule out MI.

TRIAGE_LEVEL: EMERGENT

CARE_SETTING: INPATIENT

Serial troponin measurement (baseline, 3-hour, 6-hour) with continuous cardiac monitoring
Reason: Essential to definitively rule out cocaine-induced myocardial infarction given acute presentation with chest pain, diaphoresis, and recent cocaine use.

TRIAGE_LEVEL: EMERGENT

CARE_SETTING: INPATIENT

Addiction treatment program (intensive outpatient or residential)
Reason: Cocaine use combined with uncontrolled hypertension and smoking creates imminent cardiac risk; structured treatment addresses root cause and provides monitoring/support for isolated patient.

TRIAGE_LEVEL: URGENT

CARE_SETTING: OUTPATIENT

Cardiology evaluation and cardiac imaging (echocardiogram, stress test, or coronary angiography as indicated)
Reason: Cocaine-induced chest pain with hypertension and smoking history requires assessment for myocardial infarction, ischemia, or structural cardiac damage.

TRIAGE_LEVEL: URGENT

CARE_SETTING: OUTPATIENT

Monitored acute coronary syndrome evaluation with serial ECGs and high-sensitivity troponins 
Reason: Cocaine-associated chest pain can cause delayed myocardial infarction despite initial symptom improvement.

TRIAGE_LEVEL: EMERGENT

CARE_SETTING: INPATIENT

Continuous telemetry, monitored stabilization, and analgesia/vasodilator therapy
Reason: Persistent severe cocaine-associated pain may reflect rapidly life-threatening cardiovascular toxicity.

TRIAGE_LEVEL: RESUSCITATION

CARE_SETTING: INPATIENT

Continuous cardiac monitoring, IV access, and airway/breathing support
Reason: Severe worsening chest pain may rapidly cause cardiovascular collapse.

TRIAGE_LEVEL: RESUSCITATION

CARE_SETTING: INPATIENT

Continuous cardiac monitoring with serial ECGs and troponins 
Reason: Detects evolving myocardial infarction, arrhythmia, or hemodynamic deterioration.

TRIAGE_LEVEL: EMERGENT

CARE_SETTING: INPATIENT

Continuous cardiac and blood-pressure monitoring with serial ECGs and troponins 
Reason: Detects evolving myocardial infarction, arrhythmia, or hypertensive complications.

TRIAGE_LEVEL: EMERGENT

CARE_SETTING: INPATIENT

Reason: Detects evolving myocardial infarction, arrhythmias, or other life-threatening complications.
